q: How does a Bhilai fabricator count the steel plate it buys in Scope 3?
title: Bhilai fabricators: steel plate in Scope 3
short: Multiply tonnes of plate bought by a per tonne factor, ideally the mill's own figure for that product. If the mill gives none, use an integrated steel average and say so. Plate is usually most of a fabricator's footprint, far more than its own welding and cutting.
audience: Structural and equipment fabricators around Bhilai and Durg buying plates and sections

ul: Purchase invoices with tonnes per grade.
Mill test certificates showing the producing mill.
Any per tonne figure the mill publishes or shares.

p: Electricity for cutting and welding, gases, and diesel for cranes and trucks. Add these to plate to get a footprint per tonne of finished structure.
If your structures are exported to the EU as CBAM goods under chapter 73, the plate becomes a precursor. Keep mill figures by heat or lot.

senseible: Senseible turns supplier invoices into a Scope 3 record with the supplier, quantity and factor behind every figure, so you can see which supplier data is still missing.
